leah: Quick check: can we agree on a single canonical proof envelope and a tiny mapping strategy so runtimes can attach suggestions safely during canaries?

marcus: Short answer: yes, but we need to be explicit about what is canonical vs advisory. Compiler artifact remains canon. Runtime proofs are advisory and must include minimal mapping info.

celine: Proposal: proof_envelope = {artifact_v, shape_hash, node_path, proof_hash, confidence, namespace}. Keep it very small.

dima: +1. Use a 64-bit proof_hash (xxh64) over (shape_hash||node_path||delta||epoch). Keep epoch monotonic per runtime to avoid replay.

leah: How does the mapping work if compiler renames nodes mid-rollout? We hit a similar inconsistency last month.

marcus: Compiler must emit an optional migration_map when a non-additive change occurs: old_path->new_path pairs. Runtime can apply mapping if artifact_v matches and migration_ttl not expired. If map absent, runtime suggestions referencing old paths are rejected.

celine: Safety rule: runtime only accepts proofs where artifact_v in {current, current-1}. Older ones are ignored. This keeps canary overlap safe.

dima: We also need a tiny async verifier in policy-service that ingests proofs and validates them against the uploaded artifact. If validation fails, the system increments metric policy.proof_validation.fail and drops the advisory.

leah: That verifier sounds good. Should it be synchronous on decision path or async post-hoc?

marcus: Make acceptance synchronous but lightweight: check proof_hash -> map to node_path via artifact index (const-time lookup). Full heavyweight checks (semantic diffs) can run async and alert. If async check fails later, we must emit rollback-suggestion and increment safety alert.

celine: Also add a confidence threshold. Default runtime confidence=0.75. Policy-service can override per-route. If confidence < threshold, advisory ignored.

dima: Performance tradeoff: the lookup table needs to be compact. Compiler should emit a small index mapping node_path->short_id (e.g., 4 bytes) inside artifact header to keep verifier fast.

leah: Example envelope sketch we can standardize on:

```json
{"artifact_v":"210","shape_hash":"8f3c1e","node_path":"region/eu/slot42","proof_hash":"0x9ab3f1c2d4","confidence":"0.81","namespace":"probe-eu-01","epoch":"167890"}
```

marcus: Good. Two more operational points: 1) compiler CI must lint for large migration_map (>200 entries) and require arch signoff. 2) runtimes must namespace keys by (artifact_v, namespace, runtime_id) so GC is simple.

celine: GC rule: keep artifact_v and artifact_v-1 keys; keys older than that are eligible for removal unless capability "cross_version_accept" is set. Add metric runtime.probe.gc.count.

dima: Edge case: collision on proof_hash. Use conservative fallback: if lookup returns multiple nodes or ambiguity, reject advisory. Collisions extremely rare with 64-bit but be safe.

leah: Action items: marcus draft verifier API + perf budget; celine add envelope schema to compiler output and CI lints; dima prototype runtime namespacing + epoch handling. I'll schedule a 30m arch review after drafts.

infra-bot: build:policy-compiler 2.5 -> staging (canary 5%) :white_check_mark: <https://ci/redwood/890123>

marcus: Will include two short examples: latency-preferring advisory accepted flow, and cost-preferring low-confidence rejected flow, so we can test the verifier metrics.

leah: Thanks all. Keep messages terse in the RFC so reviewers can skim.
